items.editor_note: Compared typed decision models with a classical baseline and a generative LLM for inbox routing.

editorial.tldr: Typed decision models return a probability over caller-defined options instead of generating text, and papers began placing them in agent systems as guardrails. The first paper showed an attack on that role; a security-triage study followed.
editorial.whats_new: A paper on routing a personal multilingual inbox compares typed decision models against a classical baseline and a generative LLM, arguing to measure before training.
editorial.why_it_matters: Typed decision heads are being proposed as guardrails and routers, so platform engineers need to know both how they can be attacked and how they compare with simpler baselines.
editorial.take_for_builders: If a typed decision model gates agent actions, test its option definitions for adversarial wording and benchmark it against a classical baseline before training.

status.detail: Three papers in 15 days cover an attack, a security-triage application, and a baseline comparison for typed decision models.
